I wrote the answer to `answer.json`. I worked it out by reading the code, since nothing can be run in this environment. Right before the join, `escaped_parts` is:

```
["pre\`one\`", "${state.value}", "\`mid\`literal\`", "${items.map((x) => `${x.id}", "\`)}\`tail\`end"]
```

In the JSON file, each backslash is written twice (`\\`), as JSON requires.

**How the string splits:** the pattern `\$\{.*?\}` stops at the first `}` it finds. So the nested template produces the piece `${items.map((x) => `${x.id}`, and the remaining text, starting with the backtick right after it, becomes the last outside piece.

**Pieces outside `${...}`:** the function first turns any existing `` \` `` back into a plain backtick, then escapes every backtick. An already-escaped backtick therefore stays escaped once and doesn't get a second backslash.

**`${...}` pieces:** these are left as they are.

When joined, these pieces give exactly the string the test expects, which supports the result.
